summary: 밤에 활동하는 텃새로, 백두산 고산 지대에 사는 것으로 알려져 있다. 강원도와 경기도에서 자주 관찰되고 충청도에서도 관찰된 적이 있다. 산림 개발로 서식지가 줄고 조각나면서 위협받고 있다.

art.subject: Ural Owl (Strix uralensis), adult (sexes alike), as seen in Korean mountain forests: overall pale greyish-white to pale grey-brown with only a faint buff tinge; large rounded facial disc plain pale grey, unmarked, with a thin dark-dotted rim; upperparts grey-brown with dark brown streaks and large whitish blotches at the tips of the scapulars and wing coverts; underparts greyish-white with long, narrow dark brown streaks and no cross-bars; tail long, barred dark and pale. Bill yellow; eyes small for an owl and dark brown; legs and toes densely feathered pale greyish-buff.
art.pose: perched upright on a branch at dusk
art.scene: Korean mountain forest; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, front view perched: large round head, plain pale facial disc with a thin dark rim, small dark eyes, yellow bill, pale buff underparts with long dark streaks and no cross-bars
adult, side view perched: buff-brown upperparts with dark streaks and white blotches at the feather tips, long barred tail extending well beyond the wingtips
art.build: Large owl, much bigger than a Tawny Owl and about the size of a crow, with a big rounded head without ear tufts. Bill short, hooked, yellow. Tail long and graduated, extending well beyond the folded wingtips, noticeably longer than in Tawny Owl. Perches upright and still, often on an open branch. In flight long broad wings and a long tail give a buzzard-like outline.
avoid: Do not give it ear tufts.
Do not paint large yellow or orange eyes; the eyes are relatively small and dark.
Do not paint cross-barred streaks on the underparts or a short tail; those belong to Tawny Owl (Strix aluco).
Do not paint a dark, strongly marked face; the facial disc is plain and pale.
